major_features: dotenv contract parsing
source reference scanning
CI-friendly JSON output
name: Env Sentinel
problem: Environment-variable usage, example contracts, and local configuration drift apart and cause late deployment failures.
purpose: A dependency-free local CLI that statically scans source references and compares key names with dotenv contract and configuration files without exposing values.

major_features: Interactive canvas with drag-and-drop text overlays
Real-time relative luminance mapping for gradients and images
Instant WCAG AA/AAA compliance scoring and color suggestions
name: Contrast Canvas
problem: Testing WCAG accessibility contrast ratios for complex UI components like gradients, text over images, and multi-state buttons is tedious with standard single-color pickers.
purpose: A local-first visual canvas where users can paste mockups, apply dynamic CSS gradients, overlay text elements, and instantly view a live, multi-point WCAG AA/AAA contrast map showing exactly which pixels fail contrast requirements.

major_features: Interactive visual grid of formatting anomalies
Automatic column data-type inference and mismatch highlighting
Instant export of sanitized CSV files with encoding repairs
name: CSV Schema Guard
problem: Incoming CSV files frequently have malformed rows, mismatched column counts, encoding glitches, or inconsistent date formats that break database import scripts.
purpose: A completely local browser application where users drop a CSV file to instantly get a visual audit map of structural anomalies, duplicate headers, type mismatches (e.g., text in a numeric column), and non-ASCII character highlights, with one-click repair and export.

major_features: Interactive 12-month calendar run-time projection
Confrontation detector for overlapping schedule configurations
Human-readable natural language translation of cron syntax
name: Cron Horizon
problem: Cron expressions are hard to read, debug, and predict, leading to unexpected job execution times or resource-heavy overlaps.
purpose: A local-first cron visualizer that parses standard cron syntax, generates an interactive 12-month calendar projection, and flags potential concurrency conflicts.

major_features: Interactive node-by-node path coordinate debugger
Precision decimal rounder with live visual canvas preview
Absolute-to-relative command converter
name: PathPurge SVG
problem: Exported SVGs contain bloated paths, redundant commands, and excessive decimal precision that increase asset size and complicate CSS animations.
purpose: A local-first SVG editor that parses path data, displays an interactive visual canvas showing control points, and provides granular sliders to adjust decimal precision, toggle relative/absolute commands, and instantly export optimized SVG code.

major_features: Sequential binary Write-Ahead Log (WAL) with transactional durability and crash-recovery logic
Active memory-table (MemTable) implemented using a concurrent skip-list data structure
SSTable writer and reader that converts MemTables to immutable on-disk sorted files with sparse block indexes
Background Size-Tiered Compaction Engine utilizing Java 21 Virtual Threads to merge overlapping SSTables
Custom serialized bitset-based Bloom Filters built for each SSTable segment to prevent redundant disk reads
SQL-like parser supporting SELECT, INSERT, DELETE, and WHERE clauses operating on byte-serialized row schemas
Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) implementing snapshot isolation for concurrent readers and writers
Dynamic memory budget monitor that automatically triggers MemTable flushes when threshold allocations are breached
name: AetherKV
problem: Traditional relational databases are too heavy for resource-constrained local systems, while standard key-value stores lack the ability to run structured SQL-like queries or handle high-throughput write bursts without severe latency spikes.
purpose: A zero-dependency Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM) storage engine written in Java 21. It features a binary Write-Ahead Log (WAL), size-tiered background compaction, Bloom filters, and a custom SQL-like query engine that processes tabular schemas directly on raw byte arrays.

major_features: Custom context-switching engine using platform-specific assembly and ucontext.h primitives
M:N multi-threaded scheduler mapping M green threads onto N OS worker threads
Lock-free work-stealing task queues using atomic compare-and-swap (CAS) operations
Coroutine-safe synchronization primitives including custom Mutexes, Semaphores, and Condition Variables
Preemptive interrupt engine utilizing OS interval timers (setitimer) and signal handlers to prevent infinite loops
Non-blocking I/O multiplexer integrating an epoll/kqueue wrapper directly into the scheduler loop
Thread-safe channels (both buffered and unbuffered) for message-passing between green threads
Dynamic runtime deadlock detection using a directed dependency graph of active resource locks
name: VortexScheduler
problem: Operating system threads incur high context-switching overhead, while existing async/await runtimes hide the scheduling mechanics, making deterministic concurrency debugging and priority inversion mitigation impossible.
purpose: A zero-dependency, user-space M:N coroutine scheduler and runtime built in C11. It features cooperative and preemptive green threads, lock-free work-stealing queues, custom context-switching routines, and a custom epoll-based I/O multiplexer.

major_features: Custom lexer and recursive-descent parser producing an explicit Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)
Bytecode compiler translating AST nodes into a dense stream of numeric opcodes and constant pool entries
Stack-based execution engine with explicit operand stack, call stack, and frame pointer registers
Heap allocator supporting dynamic object allocation with header metadata and type tagging
Custom mark-and-sweep garbage collector running deterministic root-set tracing and memory reclamation
Symbol table and lexical scope resolver supporting nested block scopes and variable shadowing
Built-in native function binding interface for calling host routines from bytecode instructions
Disassembler subsystem converting compiled bytecode binary streams back into human-readable assembly mnemonics
name: ByteScript VM
problem: Higher-level runtimes hide memory management, instruction execution cycles, and stack-frame layout, making it difficult to study or execute custom bytecode architectures locally.
purpose: A zero-dependency stack-based virtual machine and compiler implemented in C11. It tokenizes, parses, and compiles a statically-typed subset of language constructs into custom bytecode, executes them on an explicit heap-and-stack runtime, and runs a custom mark-and-sweep garbage collector.

major_features: Inverted index builder with positional postings lists for phrase matching
Custom English Porter Stemmer and tokenizer implementing word normalization
Sparse BM25 scoring engine calculating term frequency and inverse document frequency
Dense vector index using Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) for high-dimensional cosine similarity
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) rank merger with configurable hyper-parameters
On-disk binary serialization layout with CRC32 integrity verification
Boolean query parser supporting nested AND, OR, and NOT operators
Dynamic document update and deletion mechanics updating both sparse and dense indexes in-place
name: VeloSearch
problem: Standard vector databases are heavy and lack integrated lexical search, while traditional search engines require complex external services and fail to provide hybrid retrieval without substantial overhead.
purpose: A zero-dependency hybrid vector-lexical search engine written in Python 3.12. It features a custom BM25 index, a custom Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) dense vector index, and a Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) engine to combine semantic and keyword results.

major_features: Custom SQL lexer and AST parser supporting projection, filtering, and aggregate JOIN queries
Columnar binary file writer with run-length encoding (RLE) and dictionary compression schemes
Cost-Based Optimizer (CBO) translating ASTs to physical execution plans using catalog histograms
Physical execution engine implementing the Volcano Iterator model (open/next/close) over column chunks
Hybrid Hash Join and Sort-Merge Join algorithms operating directly on memory-mapped column buffers
Vectorized execution operator processing blocks of values to minimize virtual method call overhead
Dynamic transactional schema evolution engine supporting column addition, deletion, and renaming
Parallel column scan orchestrator utilizing Java 21 Virtual Threads for concurrent block retrieval
name: ColumnaDB
problem: Row-oriented databases struggle with analytical aggregation queries (OLAP) because they must load entire rows into memory, wasting massive I/O bandwidth on unused columns.
purpose: A zero-dependency columnar database engine written in Java 21. It implements custom binary storage structures, Run-Length Encoding (RLE), dictionary compression, a Cost-Based Optimizer (CBO) utilizing table statistics, and a Volcano-style vectorized execution model.

major_features: Leader election with randomized election timeouts managed by Java 21 Virtual Threads.
Log replication with index and term matching rules to enforce consensus agreement.
On-disk binary commit-log format featuring CRC32 checksum validation for corruption detection.
Zero-copy transfer implementation utilizing NIO FileChannel and SocketChannel primitives.
State machine replication loop executing basic key-value operations deterministically.
Cluster membership change protocol supporting joint consensus for dynamic node configuration.
Log compaction and snapshotting engine to prevent infinite log growth on disk.
Dynamic network partition injector simulating packet loss, reordering, and socket delays locally.
name: DistribuLog
problem: Traditional distributed logs rely on heavy external runtimes (like ZooKeeper) and struggle with high-throughput, low-latency replication on modern multi-core hardware.
purpose: A zero-dependency, local-consensus replicated write-ahead log using Java 21 Virtual Threads. It implements a custom raft-like consensus protocol over loopback TCP sockets, utilizing non-blocking SocketChannels and on-disk binary log structures.
